sources: https://www.nps.gov/jotr/planyourvisit/camping-outside-of-the-park.htm (read 2026-11-26, last updated May 11, 2026): 'Dispersed Camping - There are some camping options nearby the park on public lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM)... There are no developed facilities in dispersed camping areas: no restrooms, no water, no trash collection. Bring what you need and pack out all your trash... Campfires require a permit available from BLM offices. Camping is allowed within the dispersed camping areas shown, except within 300 feet (91 m) of roadways or if there are signs marking the area closed to camping.'; 'Map of BLM Dispersed Camping Area South of the Park - The BLM land south of the park allows for camping on certain sections of the BLM land. Follow the map carefully when choosing a campsite'

NPS map https://www.nps.gov/jotr/planyourvisit/images/Southth_BLM_Map_LowQuality_1.jpg (read 2026-11-26): 'BLM Dispersed Camping Areas' shaded in blocks on both sides of Cottonwood Springs Road between the park boundary and I-10 and south of I-10 - one block between MWD Aqueduct Road and Edison Power Line Road (unpaved) west of Cottonwood Springs Road, another east of it; Cottonwood Springs Road paved to the park ('To Cottonwood Visitor Center 5 mi')
https://www.blm.gov/office/palm-springs-south-coast-field-office (read 2026-11-26): field office page, phone 760-833-7100; no page for this dispersed area found
recreation.gov search (CA) for the area (read 2026-11-26): no listing

Esri World_Imagery 5 km and 1 km frames at 33.6744,-115.8023 (viewed 2026-11-26): the pin is on the west side of paved Cottonwood Springs Road just south of the MWD aqueduct road; graded dirt roads run east-west through open creosote flats with a dozen-plus parked RVs/vehicles and cleared pull-offs scattered along them on both sides of Cottonwood Springs Road

note: BLM dispersed camping on open creosote flats just south of Joshua Tree NP's Cottonwood entrance, off I-10 exit 168 on Cottonwood Springs Rd, about 5 mi below the Cottonwood Visitor Center; the paved road leads to graded dirt roads (MWD Aqueduct and Edison Power Line roads) with open pull-offs. Camp only inside the blocks on the park's BLM map and at least 300 ft from roads. No facilities; pack out trash. Campfires need a BLM permit. --Claude
summary: Joshua Tree BLM South Dispersed (BLM Palm Springs-South Coast FO): agency source found - NPS 'Camping Outside of the Park' page and its map of BLM dispersed camping areas south of the park; no designated sites (open dispersed blocks, 300 ft from roads), graded dirt roads, RVs parked there on imagery; free, first-come, no rec.gov; keep; website -> NPS page.
flags: INCLUSION: no designated individual sites - an agency-mapped dispersed camping area (NPS map 'BLM Dispersed Camping Areas', 'Camping is allowed within the dispersed camping areas shown, except within 300 feet (91 m) of roadways'). Esri imagery shows RVs and trailers on cleared pull-offs along the graded MWD Aqueduct/Edison Power Line roads, so a 23-ft rig fits; no agency 4WD or high-clearance wording. Keep.

WEBSITE: https://www.blm.gov/office/palm-springs-south-coast-field-office -> https://www.nps.gov/jotr/planyourvisit/camping-outside-of-the-park.htm (the only agency page that describes and maps this area). Phone 760-833-7100 confirmed (BLM field office).

PIN: stored 33.67440,-115.80230 is on the edge of the mapped NW block, ~40 m off paved Cottonwood Springs Road (camping must be 300 ft from roads; the pin itself is fine as a locator). Under 250 m; optional move ~250 m west into the block, e.g. 33.6744,-115.8050.
SPLIT note: the NPS map shows separate dispersed blocks east of Cottonwood Springs Road and south of I-10; they are the same agency area, ~1-3 km apart, not separate campgrounds.
